content.user_title: Design Testable Go Services With Dependency Injection
content.value_statement: Hidden dependencies and global state make Go services difficult to test and maintain. This skill guides constructor injection, library selection, and incremental refactoring with practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Explain constructor injection and consumer-defined interfaces using Go service examples.
Compare manual wiring, google/wire, uber-go/dig, uber-go/fx, and samber/do.
Guide refactoring of global dependencies, implicit initialization, and service-locator patterns.
Illustrate startup wiring, Fx lifecycle hooks, and service shutdown patterns.
Demonstrate interface mocks, dependency overrides, and service testing.
Show Wire provider sets, build constraints, and generated constructor wiring.
limitations: Examples are instructional fragments, not complete applications ready for deployment.
Library APIs require verification against current official documentation and installed versions.
The full samber/do API and advanced features are delegated to a separate skill.
Parallel refactoring analysis depends on agent support in the host environment.

use_cases.title: Start a Small Go API
use_cases.description: Arrange configuration, repositories, services, and handlers with explicit constructors instead of introducing a container prematurely.
use_cases.target_user: Go developers building their first service

use_cases.title: Refactor Coupled Services
use_cases.description: Identify globals, implicit initialization, and container lookups, then plan an incremental migration to explicit dependencies.
use_cases.target_user: Backend maintainers working on existing Go applications

use_cases.title: Select a DI Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare code generation, reflection, generics, lifecycle support, and testing approaches for a growing service architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Learn Constructor Injection
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain constructor injection for a Go UserService that needs a UserStore and logger. Show consumer-defined interfaces and manual wiring without a DI library.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Service Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Go tests for a UserService using a mock UserStore. Cover found and missing users without a real database or DI library.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: isolate a service for unit testing.

prompt_templates.title: Compare DI Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare manual wiring, Wire, Dig, Fx, and samber/do for my Go application. Ask about service count, lifecycle needs, and team preferences before recommending.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: choose a suitable wiring strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dependency Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go project for globals, init-based service setup, and service-locator patterns. Map dependencies and propose an incremental migration with tests and shutdown handling.

output_examples.input: Which DI approach fits a Go API with five services?
output: Use manual constructor injection rather than a DI library.
Initialize configuration and infrastructure before repositories, services, and handlers.
Keep dependencies explicit and inject mocks for unit tests.

output_examples.input: My UserService receives a container and looks up its database.
output: This is a service-locator pattern that hides the service dependencies.
Change the constructor to accept the specific database interface.
Keep container resolution at application startup and test the service with a mock.

output_examples.input: How should Fx manage a database connection?
output: Register a lifecycle hook in the database provider.
Connect during startup and close the connection during shutdown.
Use context-aware hooks and verify behavior with the Fx testing package.

best_practices: Start with manual constructor injection when the dependency graph is small.
Define interfaces where consumed and keep container access at the composition root.
Verify library APIs against current documentation and test dependency failures and resource cleanup.
anti_patterns: Using global variables or init functions to create service dependencies.
Passing a DI container into business services for dependency lookup.
Creating a complete application container for every HTTP request.

faq.question: Do I need a DI library for a small Go project?
faq.answer: Usually not. The skill recommends manual constructor injection for small projects with simple dependencies.

faq.question: Which DI libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It compares google/wire, uber-go/dig, uber-go/fx, and samber/do alongside manual wiring.

faq.question: Can this skill help refactor existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Its refactor workflow identifies globals, implicit initialization, concrete dependencies, and service-locator patterns before proposing a migration.

faq.question: Does the skill cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes manual mock injection, container override examples, and an Fx testing example.

faq.question: Are the examples complete and guaranteed to compile?
faq.answer: No. They omit application-specific definitions and require checking library signatures, registrations, and installed versions.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares compatibility with Claude Code and Codex; tool availability depends on the host environment.
